title: YM2149
body:
[[PSG]] Handler

The Atari ST's sound chip, and a [[PSG]] rather than a sample player: three square-wave tone
channels plus one noise channel, driven by writing [[Frequency]] and [[Amplitude]] values
into its registers. It costs almost no [[CPU]] time because the chip generates the waveform
itself.

It also carries some unrelated I/O on its spare port lines (the parallel port, floppy drive
select), which is the sort of thing that happens when a system has more signals than chips.

[[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]] does the sound side properly: [[Sound]], [[PCM]], [[DAC's and ADC's]].

[[Motorola 68000]] · [[6850 ACIA]] · [[68901 MFP]] · [[GLUE]] · [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]]
